title: Bradykinesia in Parkinson's
content: Bradykinesia means slowness of movement and is one of the characteristic movement features of Parkinson's disease. It can make everyday activities take longer and may cause difficulty initiating or continuing movements. A person may notice smaller movements, reduced facial expression, decreased arm swing while walking, difficulty getting out of a chair, or challenges with repetitive tasks such as buttoning clothes. Handwriting may become smaller. Bradykinesia can affect walking and contribute to short or shuffling steps. Slowness of movement can have causes other than Parkinson's disease and should be assessed together with other symptoms and clinical findings.
